A. About   Vijaybhoomi University 
 
Vijaybhoomi University is India’s first liberal 
university, which aspires to offer  relevant      
and quality education and engage in high-
quality research. It is  also Maharashtra’s first 
greenfield university. The university, based in 
Karjat, Raigad, is devoted to nurturing holistic, 
socially responsible, and continuously 
employable professionals who make a 
positive difference in the world. We focus on 
making an individual “industry-ready” along 
with developing a personality ready to     
face and transcend any challenge in any 
niche. 
The curriculum at Vijaybhoomi 
University is based on the Multiple 
Intelligence framework. It is a fully 
choice based credit system having 
international pathways to partners such 
 
as the State University of New York, 
Paris School of Business and University of 
Wollongong, Australia. 
Vijaybhoomi is promoted by Dalal 
Street Investment Journal (DSIJ), 
Jagdish Sheth School of Management 
(JAGSoM), formerly known as IFIM 
Business School) and IFIM Institutions. DSIJ, 
having its head office in Mumbai was 
founded in 1986. JAGSoM, with its campus in 
Bangalore was founded in 1995. Today, 
JAGSoM is ranked among the top 30 business 
schools in India and is now accredited by the 
world’s gold standard in business school 
accreditations – Association to Advance 
Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)`, 
making it one among the first six schools in 
India to achieve this honour. 
B. Spirit of Vijay – 
Our values and 
guiding 
principles 
 
 
● Value integrity and earn others’ trust. 
 
● Innovate continuously and be agile. 
 
● Jettison fear of failure and learn from 
mistakes. 
 
● Appreciate your origins and build on them 
to be a good citizen. 
 
● Yield not to unethical shortcuts and be 
socially responsible. 
 
C. Vision 
To be the most sought-after destination 
 
for liberal professional education 
 
D. Mission 
Nurture holistic, socially responsible, and 
continuously employable 
professionals.

E. Student –Rules and 
Regulations 
1. Scope 
1.1 Vijaybhoomi University is 
committed to providing an inspiring 
and intellectually stimulating and safe 
environment, with a culture of respect 
for all members of the university 
community. By choosing to become 
members of this community, students, 
staff, and faculty affirm their 
commitment to its philosophy, ethos 
and values and understand the 
responsibility placed upon them. 
1.2 To maintain its values and culture 
the University has formed rules and 
regulations violations of which will 
jeopardize its environment. Hence to 
enforce discipline and student conduct 
on campus the University will enforce 
its Rules and Regulations. 
1.3 The said rules are subject to 
review/alterations/modifications/ 
additions /deletions, either in part or 
whole at any time hereafter, at the 
exclusive discretion of the 
Management. Students are required to 
read and be aware of all notices that 
are put up on the Notice Boards. 
1.4 It must be expressly understood that 
the University or its nominees shall not 
be held responsible in any manner 
whatsoever in case of any injury and/ or 
loss of life or belongings of any hostel 
residents due to theft, burglary, fire, 
riot, or any natural calamity or 
circumstances whatsoever. 
1.5 The rules outlined in the Student 
Handbook apply equally to both day 
scholars and students residing in 
campus hostels. 
2. Disciplinary Committee (DC) 
2.1 At  Vijaybhoomi University, we want to 
ensure a respectful and supportive 
environment for all members, 
including students, faculty, and staff. If you 
have concerns about a fellow 
student violating our university’s rules and 
regulations, we encourage you to reach out 
to our Disciplinary Committee (DC) to 
address the issue. The DC will deal with 
non-cognizable offences and established 
offences wherein the student has repeated 
the offence and exhausted all the provided 
chances and fine options. 
2.2 Constitution of the DC 
The disciplinary committee (DC)  has been 
constituted by the                                                                Vice 
Chancellor as follows: 
2.2.1   Director – Sports & Student 
Experience / Student Affairs: as

2.3   The DC’s decision shall be final. A 
student shall have the right to make an 
appeal with the Ombudsman of University 
in case the alleged student(s) are not 
satisfied by the proceedings for the DC and 
the outcome of the DC’s deliberation. 
3.  Filing Complaints with DC 
3.1 To initiate the process, please submit 
your complaint in writing to the DC email 
address (disciplinarycommittee@ 
Vijaybhoomi. edu.in) within three working 
days of the incident. The Registrar’s office is 
obligated to initiate such proceedings of the 
DC in cases where the student has exhausted 
the maximum number of fine options 
provided against each of the cognizable 
offences mentioned herein. 
3.2 Once the DC receives your written 
complaint, the DC will conduct a 
preliminary investigation to determine its 
validity. The DC shall inform both the 
complainant and the defendant of the 
outcome of their preliminary decision 
within five working days. 
3.3 If the complaint is deemed valid, the 
DC will proceed with a thorough 
examination. This step will involve 
requesting a written statement from the 
defendant and offering them the option of a 
verbal hearing if desired. We expect the 
defendant to acknowledge receipt of the 
complaint and provide their written 
statement within 72 hours, though they can 
request an extension if needed, subject to 
the Committee’s discretion. 
3.4 After these initial steps, the DC will 
initiate deliberations to determine the 
defendant’s culpability and decide on any 
appropriate consequences or penalties. We 
pledge to communicate the final decision to 
all parties within 4 weeks of accepting the 
case. 
3.5 In cases involving suspension or 
expulsion, we will notify the defendant and 
their parents or guardians through the 
Registrar’s office. All other decisions will be 
communicated to the defendant by the Chair 
of the DC, with the complainant also being 
informed of the outcome. The Registrar 
may share information with relevant 
university offices and authorities as 
necessary. 
3.6   Please note that the DC reserves the 
right to proceed with a case in absentia if 
the defendants or witnesses fail to respond 
within the specified timelines. 
4.  Decisions of DC 
We believe in conducting disciplinary 
proceedings with fairness, though they  do 
not follow the same rules as a court of law. 
The legal rules of evidence do 
not apply, and the DC may use any 
relevant information, including 
hearsay and third-party testimony. 
In cases where penalties are imposed, 
parents or guardians will be notified, but 
this will primarily apply to suspension or 
expulsion orders. In exceptional 
circumstances advised by the DC, 
notifications may also be sent  for other 
penalties. Decisions regarding violations 
will be based on a careful consideration of 
all available information, using the standard 
of preponderance of probabilities. 
 
5.  Defendant and Complainant  
During DC proceedings, defendants, 
complainants, and witnesses have 
certain rights, including access to 
university policies and procedures, 
information about pending charges, 
freedom from intimidation, and 
protection from unwarranted searches or

seizures. The DC emphasize the     
importance   of confidentiality 
throughout the disciplinary process, 
and all parties 
involved are expected to maintain this 
confidentiality. The DC will always allow  a 
minimum of 24 hours for responses in 
communications with the parties involved, 
with the possibility of extensions granted at 
the discretion of the Committee. 
 
6. Appeals 
If parties wish to appeal the DC’s 
decision, they have the right to do so  
within five working days, provided 
they state clear grounds for their  appeal. 
The appeals will need to  be made to the 
Registrar of the University in writing. 
Appeals will be considered in cases 
involving new evidence or significant 
procedural errors. The Registrar will 
consult the Vice Chancellor for accepting 
the appeals. In case the same is accepted 
the complainant and the defendant will be 
informed by the Registrar office providing 
the details of the Appeals Committee 
which will be chaired by the Vice Chancellor 
or 
his/her 
nominee. 
The 
appeals 
committee will conduct its deliberations 
under the guidance and directions of the 
VC. A decision taken by the appeals 
committee will be final and binding on the 
complainant 
and 
the 
defendant. 
 
7. Documentation 
Documentation of all cases referred to  the 
DC will be maintained for at least 
two 
years from the date of the final decision. 
8. Rules for Student Staying on Campus 
8.1 Checking in / Checking out of Campus. 
8.1.1 Students be allowed to check in into 
the campus by 6:00 AM and check out of the 
university campus by 09.00 PM (herein after 
called day hours) unless special permission 
has been granted by the competent 
authority. 
8.1.2 
The campus security maintains a 
movement register and all students exiting 
the gates of the University during the 
permitted time are required  to sign out and 
sign in whilst entering the campus. 
8.1.3 The movement register will be 
available with security only during the day 
hours. For the remaining period the register 
will be in the possession of the warden. 
8.1.3    In case a student for any reason 
whatsoever enters or exits the campus 
outside of the day hours, the security will 
inform this to the warden.  
8.1.5 In accordance with the regulations set 
forth by the university Registrar/Warden/ 
Admin Dept. students who plan to depart 
from the hostel for an extended period, 
specifically for a duration of overnight or 
longer, or during scheduled term breaks, 
must make an application to the warden in 
the prescribed format along with the 
consent of the parent or 
the 
local 
guardian. 
This 
application 
should 
be 
submitted 48hours in advance. 
8.1.6   On being permitted to leave the 
campus for the approved period, the student 
needs to lock his belongings in  the 
provided 
storage space and exit the campus by signing 
out in the register at the security.  
  8.1.7 No students will be allowed to enter the 
campus in an inebriated state. If a student is 
found in such a state, the security will take the

student 
to 
the 
infirmary 
for 
an 
immediate check up by the CMO or the 
nurse. In case the student is found to 
have consumed  alcohol or any form of a 
reactional drug/narcotic substances, the 
CMO shall immediately inform the  
warden. The student will not be 
permitted to enter the hostel room in this 
state will be required to rest in the 
infirmary till permitted by the CMO to 
use the hostel room. State of inebriation 
is a punishable offence. 
8.1.9   Before leaving for the term break or for 
the purpose explained prior, students are 
required to vacate their allocated beds and 
rooms. 
 
9. Term Break and Storing of   
personal luggage. 
9.1.  The University conducts room 
maintenance during term breaks, so 
students must store their belongings in 
designated areas identified by the 
Warden and managed by the VP-DORF 
(Student Council). The Warden, in 
consultation with the CAO, will ensure at 
least two rooms are set aside for 
storage, including the shooting range 
room near the Gym and a separate room 
for musical instruments. The VP-DORF 
and their team will organize the storage 
area, tag items, maintain a storage list, 
and lock the storage rooms. The keys will 
be held by the VP-DORF and the 
Warden/CAO. At the start of the next 
term, the VP-DORF will help students 
retrieve their belongings and move them 
to their new rooms. While the University 
will try to keep students in the same 
rooms for up to four terms, this is not 
guaranteed. 
9.2 Responsibility for Luggage: If students do 
not follow the storage guidelines, the 
University will not be responsible for any loss 
or damage. Students must follow the 
instructions from the hostel authorities and 
Student Council and take steps to protect their 
belongings. The Student Council is in charge of 
transporting and managing stored luggage. 
Unclaimed luggage will be kept for up to three 
months, after which a board, including Student 
Council members, will decide how to dispose 
of it. 
10. Hostel Orders 
10.1 Occupancy Terms: Staying in the hostel 
doesn’t grant tenancy rights. Your stay is 
subject to University Rules, which may change 
at any time. Violations will lead to disciplinary 
action as outlined in the Vijaybhoomi 
University Student Handbook. 
10.2   Rules Display: Hostel rules will be 
posted in common areas for easy reference. 
10.3     Cleanliness Issues: Report any 
cleanliness issues in the register available at 
the security desk. 
10.4 Mess Information: Notify the mess a day 
in advance if you won’t be dining there. 
10.5 Service During Illness: Room service for 
food is only allowed if   approved by the 
campus doctor. 
10.6         Fortnightly Inspections: The Hostel 
Committee will conduct inspections every two 
weeks and address any concerns. 
10.7         Suggestion Box: A suggestion box will 
be placed near the hostel security desk and 
checked biweekly in the presence of the 
Campus Administrator and a student 
representative. 
11.  Room Orders 
 
11.1 Room Allocation: Students of the same 
gender will be assigned to the same room. No 
students of one gender are allowed to visit the 
room of the other gender at any time of the day

or night. Breaching this rule is a 
punishable offence. Rooms are allocated 
on a temporary basis. Students must 
adhere to the specific period mentioned 
for their room allocation.  
11.2 Room Changes: Students cannot 
change or interchange rooms without 
written permission from the CAO or 
Warden. The CAO or Warden can reassign 
rooms at any time without explanation. 
11.3 Locks and Keys: Students must use 
the Laches fixed in their cupboard to keep 
personal belongings and valuables under 
lock and key. Room keys are maintained 
by the hostel, and the main key will be 
given to a designated student of each 
room. That student will be solely 
responsible for the key and will be liable 
to be penalized Rs. 1000/- if lost / 
misplaced.

11.5 Staying in Hostel after Submitting Exit 
Forms: No students who have submitted 
their exit form are allowed to stay inside 
the campus overnight. Even in the case of 
submission of SIP or of Internship related 
reports there is no scope for such students 
to stay inside the campus.  These types of 
requests will not to be recommended by 
any staff / faculty.

13. Reporting back to Campus. 
13.1   Reporting back should be done so 
between 0800AM and 0900PM on the 
date of reporting back. 
13.2   Accordingly, the students should 
plan travel so that they report back to 
campus not later than 0900PM on the 
date of reporting back. 
13.3   In case of delay in reporting back, 
the student must apply for extension of 
leave by email to respective school Dean 
with copy to Warden. On approval the dean will 
inform the student by return email along with 
copy to Warden and security.  Security will 
accordingly allow the student into the campus 
as per the new reporting date. 
14. 
Time for Departure from Campus 
14.1   Students are allowed to leave campus on 
leave between 0600AM and 0900PM. 
14.2   The students may be permitted to leave 
campus beyond 0900PM only if parents have 
come to pick up the students.  
14.3 The students should plan their journey 
ahead by flight/ train etc. keeping in mind the 
exit time from campus. 
 
      15. Disciplinary Orders 
15.1 Check- in Time: Students must return to 
campus by 09:00 PM. A 30-minute grace period 
is allowed. Students arriving late for the first 
time will be warned. Students coming late for 
the second time and onwards will incur a Rs. 
500/-fine per night and their parents will be 
informed. 
15.2 On Fridays and Saturdays students may 
report back to campus by 11:00PM but not later 
than that. However, on Sundays students will 
have to return to campus by 09:00PM as there 
are regular classes on the following day. 
15.3 Attendance: Students must sign the 
attendance register by 10:30 PM. 
15.4  Prohibited Activities: No gambling, 
firearms, ammunition, explosives, alcohol, 
drugs, or smoking is allowed on hostel 
premises. Violations will result in severe 
disciplinary actions, including rustication. 
15.5 Dress Code: As given out in the Students 
Handbook proper attire must be worn in the 
library, classrooms, and dining hall. 
Inappropriate attire will invite penalties as per 
the Students Handbook.

15.6   Checking by Security: All baggage 
and goods brought into the  hostel room 
are subject to be checked by the security 
on the instructions of the warden. 
University reserves the right to disallow 
possession of items in the rooms and the 
warden will have the final say on such a 
decision. Please note this would include 
goods ordered from E-commerce platforms. 
 
15.7 Consumption of Food in Hostel 
room: Students cannot bring food from the 
mess to their rooms. They are required 
 
to consume their food only in the 
student mess area or other designated 
areas. Students can order food from 
outside; however, students are required to 
consume this food in either the student 
mess or other designated areas. 
Consumption of cooked food inside the 
hostel room is strictly prohibited. 
15.8   Pets: Keeping pets in the hostel is 
strictly prohibited. In case a student is 
found in possession of a pet inside the 
hostel, the security personnel /warden 
will have the right to evict the pet from 
the  premises.  
16. Rules for Day Scholars 
16.1 The Institute timings for day 
scholars are from 9:00 AM to 5:00PM. 
16.2 The day scholars are expected to 
reach the Institute by 9:00 AM to avoid 
loss of attendance of the first lecture. 
16.3 Students must have a University ID 
Card in person when on campus. 
16.4   Day Scholars are not permitted to 
enter the hostel complex. 
16.5   The dress code as given in this 
student handbook is also applicable to Days 
Scholars. 
16.6   In between the academic hours, lunch 
break will be there from 01:00PM to 02:15PM. 
Students may visit the canteen, cafeterias, 
grounds etc. on the premises during this period.  
16.7   The students must manage their 
attendance. Leave will only be sanctioned by 
Dean or the Director in charge only for purposes 
of representing the University in games, 
competition etc. 
16.8   Transportation facilities are available for 
day scholars. Students can avail themselves of 
the facilities by paying bus fees with the 
institute’s annual fees. All the rules and 
regulations must be followed by bus boarders; 
any misconduct may cancel their bus 
membership. 
16.9   Any visitor accompanying the student is 
not permitted to visit the campus without prior 
permission from the respective authorities of the 
institute. 
16.10University attendance and leave rules are   
applicable to Days Scholars. 
 
  17.  Use of University Assets and      
Electronic Items 
17.1 Fixtures: No extra furniture or fixtures 
allowed. Damages will result in double the 
original cost for repairs. 
17.2   Interchange of Furniture/ Fixture: No 
interchange of furniture/ fixtures between 
locations is allowed.  
       17.3 Electric Appliances: Heavy-duty 
electrical appliances like irons, 
microwaves, room   heaters, and hair 
dryers are not allowed. Any damage to 
electrical sockets or switches due to 
misuse will result in penalties and 
repair costs charged to the occupants 
of the room. 
17.4 Conserving Electricity: All students are 
required to conserve electricity by switching 
off lights, fans, Acs and other electrical 
appliances when not in use. The University

covers up to 100 units of electricity 
consumption per room per month. Any 
usage beyond this limit, especially for 
services like AC, will be the financial 
responsibility of the students of the 
designated room. Additional charges will 
be billed directly to the student’s account 
and  will  be divided equally among all 
students staying in the same room. 
17.5Internet Usage: Each student is 
allotted 150 GB of internet data per 
month at a speed of 10 Mbps. Students 
are encouraged to use the internet 
responsibly and avoid excessive usage 
that may lead to throttling or additional 
charges. In case of any issues with the 
Wi-Fi connectivity, students should 
report to the IT support team 
immediately for resolution. 
18. General Conduct: 
18.1 
Students are not permitted to 
venture out into the open areas of 
the campus without supervision at 
any point of time. Security personnel 
have the right  to request the student 
to immediately return to the 
developed areas in case they find 
students venturing in the open area. 
Defiance of such an order by the 
security personnel is a punishable 
offence. 
18.2 
Personal Display of Affection 
is a punishable offence in the 
campus. Holding hands, kissing, 
hugging, and embracing, patting and 
any such gestures between the same 
or different genders which is not 
platonic in nature shall be considered 
as PDA. All security personnel or for 
that matter any official of the 
University shall have the right to 
immediately instruct the student to refrain 
from PDA. Defiance of such an order from 
any University Official or Authorized 
personnel will be considered as a breach 
and is a punishable offence. 
18.3   Any kind of violence on campus 
between students, students and university 
officials, students and authorized 
personnel of the University is a punishable 
offence. Security personnel/University 
officials/Authorized personnel have the 
right to stop any incident of violence that 
may arise. Students   caught in any violent 
act will be punished severely. 
  18.4 Use of abusive and foul language in the 
University is not permitted. All University officials 
and authorized personnel have the right to instruct 
the student to stop using such language. Defiance 
of such an instruction is a punishable offence. 
18,5   Not adhering to the dress code as 
prescribed in this handbook can result in debarring 
the student from the area  or the activity by the 
faculty/ instructor/ administrator/ security 
personnel. Defiance of such an instruction is a 
punishable offence. 
18.6 Intentionally damaging the property of the 
institute is a punishable offence. Any student 
found engaging in this activity will be punished 
severely. 
18.7 Students need to park their vehicles in the 
designated parking zones. Defiance of such an 
order from any University Official or Authorized 
personnel will be considered as a breach and is a 
punishable offence. 
18.8 Students are not allowed to entertain any 
outsider in their hostel rooms. The VP-DORF, Hostel 
Committee members, the warden and 
administrative staff including the house keeping 
staff have the authority to instruct the students to   
immediately evict the outsider. Defiance of such 
an order from any University Official or 
Authorized personnel will be considered as a

breach and is a punishable offence. Outsider 
here implies any person other than a student 
or university official who has not been 
granted explicit permission to access the 
room. 
18.9  Residents indulging in any 
criminal, unlawful, or offensive 
activity will be punished, warned, or 
evicted from the hostel depending on 
the nature of the offense. 
18.10   Students should not use 
prohibited areas and areas outside the 
limits of student access without 
appropriate permissions. Breach of 
this rule will result in a trespassing 
offence which is punishable. 
18.11 Students must comply with the Anti- 
Ragging Regulations as stipulated by the 
laws of the country. Ragging is a serious 
offence. The definition of ragging and its 
consequences will be dealt with as per the 
UGC regulations 
stipulated in 
https://www.ugc.gov.in/oldpdf/ragging 
/minuterag230409.pdf. 
18.12  Vijaybhoomi University is a non- 
smoking/non-vaping campus, smoking/vaping 
in any part of the campus is a punishable 
offence. 
18.13   The University reserves the 
right to amend and add new rules 
and regulations. The students are 
requested to keep themselves abreast 
of such changes but actively read the 
circulars and notices issued by the 
University. 
18.14   Ignorance of these rules and 
regulations will not be considered as a 
defense when being tried for any 
punishable offence.

19. Non-Academic Punishable Offences 
Punishable offences will be of two types. 
19.1 
Cognizable Offences – Offences which are visually detected by the University 
Officials/Authorised Personnel/Security Personnel or captured on our AI enabled CCTV 
surveillance system. 
19.2       Non-Cognizable offences – Offences that are reported by other students or charges 
of mental harassment to the authority.

22.   Code of Conduct for Students. 
22.1 Dress Code: 
The students are required to adhere to the 
following dress code in all 
institutional areas and common areas of the 
campus including the dining facility. The 
dress code for using of sport arena is 
defined under the Sport and Gym facility 
section. 
22.2 Dress Code for Students – Male 
  22.2.1 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and 
Thursday: Smart casual trouser, smart casual 
shirt with full sleeves /half sleeves, Indian 
ethnic wear, appropriate footwear according 
to season. 
  22.2.2 Friday / Saturday / Sunday: Smart 
casuals. 
22.2.3 Official Event: On an official event, 
whether on campus or outside where the 
individual is representing IFIM, Formal dress 
code will apply. 
22.2.4 NOT ALLOWED: Prominent/ 
big/offensive prints on ‘T’ Shirts, Sleeveless ‘T’ 
Shirts, See-through clothing, Sandals & 
Bathroom sleepers/ chappals are strictly 
prohibited in the campus. 
22.2.5 Formal Dress for Males: Trouser and full 
sleeves shirt with closed formal shoes. Blazer/ 
jacket as appropriate if it is an occasion. 
 
22.3. Dress Code for Students – Female 
22.3.1   Monday, Tuesday,   Wednesday & 
Thursday: Western formals such as formal 
shirt with Trouser/Below Knee level skirt or 
Indian formals such as Saree/ Salwar Kameez 
with appropriate formal footwear. 
22.3.2 Friday/Saturday/Sunday: Smart 
casuals. 
22.3.3 Official Event: On an official event, 
whether on campus or outside where the 
individual is representing IFIM, Formal 
dress code will apply. 
 
22.3.4 NOT ALLOWED: Short skirts, short 
shorts, prominent and big or offensive 
prints on ‘T’ Shirts, Sleeveless ‘T’ Shirts, 
sleeveless tops, low cuts, see-through clothing, 
Spaghetti tops, Bathroom  
 
22.3.5 Chappals are  strictly prohibited on the 
campus. 
 
22.3.6 Formal Dress Code for Females:    
Western formals such as formal shirt with 
Trouser/Below Knee level skirt or Indian 
formals such as Saree/ Salwar Kameez with 
appropriate formal footwear. 
 
22.3.7 Dress Code for Transgenders 
Transgenders can follow any one of the dress 
codes mentioned above as they follow in their 
daily routine. 
 
23. Dress Code Exceptions 
 
23.1  The above dress code is applicable to 
students of all schools at all times. However, 
some schools may require the student to 
follow a specific dress code as dictated by 
the profession on some/all days. The 
schools dress code for students pursuing 
their professional courses shall supersede 
the University dress code mentioned herein. 
23.2  Students taking part in uniformed 
services such as the NCC, NSS etc may be 
required to be present in their respective 
uniforms on certain days. Such uniforms 
will supersede the University dress code on 
such days. 
23.3  Students may be exempted to wear 
formal shoes on days when they are 
nursing injuries or medical conditions in 
the feet region. 
 
24. Do’s and Don’ts 
Do’s 
24.1  Students must bring with them 
adequate numbers of bed sheets, pillow- 
covers, blanket(s) and other personal 
toiletries and amenities for their personal

use for maintaining hygiene. 
24.2 Students are expected to act 
professionally, always maintaining a 
harmonious atmosphere conducive to the 
professional well-being of everyone in the 
hostel. 
24.3 Student ID Card should be worn daily 
and should always be clearly visible in the 
campus without exception for all the 
students. 
24.4 The students must take care of hostel 
room provisions including Air Conditioner, 
lights, fans, switches/regulators/sockets, 
study table, cot, chair, cupboard, curtain rods, 
windows/doors, and most importantly – room 
keys. To save energy, students are requested 
to switch- off the electrical appliances when 
not in use. 
24.5 Students must carry a torch light whilst 
using the common areas of the campus in the 
late evening and night hours. 
24.6 Students are required to attend their 
classes regularly and punctually. 
27.7 Students must take adequate 
precautions to ensure that their personal 
belongings are not left unattended and 
unlocked to prevent theft and 
embezzlement. 
24.8 Students are required to adhere to the 
stipulated dress codes mentioned in this 
handbook. 
24.9 Students must behave like responsible 
citizens and are expected to comply with all 
the laws of the country. 
24.10   Students are required to respect 
the individuality of other students. 
24.11  Students must constructively use all the 
facilities provided by the University. 
24.12  Students living at the hostel are 
mandated to punch into the biometric 
machine or signature in the hostel 
attendance register during the off Day 
Hours. 
24.13  Students must adhere to the guidelines and 
instructions for use of any of its facilities strictly. 
24.14   Students are allowed to play 
music softly and if it does not disturb 
others. 
24.15 Students must keep their living 
areas and surroundings clean. 
24.16 Students must not litter the campus 
and wherever possible propagate 
cleanliness across the campus. 
24.17 Students must pay their dues on time 
using the keep learning platform. 
24.18 Students must read through the 
Academic Guidelines thoroughly. 
24.19 Students must read the Student Council 
Constitution and understand the organization 
of the student’s council. 
24.20 Students must attend all the orientation 
sessions and thoroughly read the various 
handbooks of Research/Innovation 
Incubation, Personality Enhancement Plan 
(PEP), Social Immersion Program (SIP), 
Miracle X (Mentoring), Industry Internship 
Program (IIP) etc. 
24.21 Students will need to be tolerant of 
disturbances caused due to events such 
 
as festivals, convocations etc. 
organized by the University. 
24.22 Students must actively participate in 
student club activities. The details of the 
clubs etc. can be understood by the 
Chairperson Student Affairs and the Student 
council members. 
 
24.23 Students are required to refrain from 
using prohibited areas such as the 
terraces of the buildings. 
 
Don’ts 
 
24.24 Students shall have to abide by the 
decisions of the hostel warden and 
University authority with respect to

enforcement of the hostel rules, failing 
which the same shall be treated as 
defiance of an instruction. 
24.25 Modifications /alternations/ 
meddling with existing structure, fittings, 
and electrical connections are strictly 
prohibited, and liable for action. 
24.26 No notice shall be put in the 
Hostel directly by any student unless 
such permission has been granted by 
the Warden or Admin Dept. 
24.27 Event posters are not allowed to be 
pasted anywhere in the hostel other than 
the notice boards. 
24.28 Students should not feed or encourage 
the presence of stray animals, such as dogs, 
cats etc., within the campus. 
24.29 Students are not permitted to watch 
pornographic or objectionable content on 
campus. 
24.30 Students should not make noise or 
sounds that disturb others. 
24.31 Students should not discriminate basis 
eating habits, religion, gender, caste, 
nationality, or creed on the campus. 
24.32 Students should not venture out into 
the open areas of the campus. 
24.33 Students must stay away from reptiles, 
insects, and other animals. In case of spotting 
a dangerous reptile/insect the students must 
immediately vacate the premises and inform 
the security personnel to address the 
situation. 
24.34 Students should stay in the hostel room 
when suffering with infectious diseases, the 
students must voluntarily report to the 
infirmary and use the facility till cured. 
24.35 Vijaybhoomi University doesn’t 
align with any political ideologies. 
Students need to refrain from 
propagating any political agendas or 
form any political parties on the 
campus. 
25. Exceptions to the Rules and 
Regulations 
25.1 Medical Conditions 
Students who are injured or ill and require 
to be hospitalized or taken care off at home 
will be absolved from the leave processes 
described above. Provided that such 
conditions are confirmed by the CMO. 
During such leave of absence, a student may 
approach the Program Office to grant a 
leave of absence for the course work in 
progress. In such cases the decision of the 
Academic Council communicated via the 
Registrar office will 
be final. 
If a student is diagnosed with illness 
and is 
prescribed to stay in the room, the student will 
be allowed to take his prescribed meals in the 
hostel room. 
25.2 On Duty 
Students representing the University in sport 
competitions, festivals, and other 
competitions can apply to the Program 
Office to grant an “On Duty” leave. In such 
cases if the Academic Council 
permits the student will be granted leave of 
absence across all courses. This  shall be 
confirmed by the Registrar provided the 
application is made at least 10 days before 
the said event and is approved by the 
Academic Council members. 
25.3 Change of Hostel Room 
The student may or may not be 
provided limited choice for selecting 
their preference of the rooms. However, under 
special circumstances associated  with medical or 
physical conditions the student may apply to the 
Registrar office for a specific room. The Registrar on 
a best effort basis will try to 
accommodate such request provided the 
condition is confirmed by the CMO. 
25.4 Environmental Conditions 
Students who exit campus during the day hours

and are not able to return in time due to lack 
of transport or 
environmental conditions will be allowed to 
use their rooms even if they arrive off day 
hours. However, this will be solely on the 
discretion of the warden on duty. Such 
students will be asked to wait at the 
administration 
block till the warden arrives or the warden 
issues a written notice to the security to 
allow the students into the campus.

 Based on the meal plan subscribed by the

University campus

noon hours.

has

comply with the rules.

27.6.1 The university has a residential Chief

27.7 Laundry Service 
27.7.1 In-house laundry service shall be 
provided at an additional cost. Every student 
is requested to make use of the same fully. 
The laundry charges are regulated and are 
available with the Vice – President – DORF 
(Student Council) and/or the Warden. The 
same is also required to be displayed in the 
laundry prominently. Students need to 
ensure that they pay as per the regulated 
charges and pay the same electronically only. 
Here are the key details you need to 
know:  
27.7.2 Operating Hours: Displayed at the 
facility. 
27.7.3 Laundry Rates: Displayed at the laundry 
facility and available with the VP-DORF and/or 
Warden. 
27.7.3 Payment Options: Electronically only. 
27.7.4 Delivery and Collection of Clothes. All 
clothes need to be delivered at the laundry facility 
during the operation 
hours in a cloth bag. Each cloth bag will be tagged 
with your name, ensuring no mix-up occurs. 
Additionally, all pieces of clothing will be 
meticulously counted and the cost for the service 
will be provided to the user in advance. Please 
ensure that all valuable items are removed from 
the pockets whilst delivering the clothes. Neither 
the University nor the Service Provider shall be 
responsible for any loss of valuables. Also note 
that expensive and branded clothes are self-
washed and ironed. 
Neither the University nor the service provider shall 
take responsibility for damage to such clothes and 
wear. 
27.7.5 Hygiene Recommendations. 
Students suffering from any infectious disease are 
required to inform the service provider before 
submitting their clothes so that the same are 
washed in isolation. 
27.7.6 Please note the service provider reserves 
the right to refuse wash/iron undergarments,

lingerie etc. Students are requested to wash 
this on them to promote hygiene and protect 
their own privacy. 
27.7.7 Optimal Laundry Load to maintain an 
efficient laundry process for everyone, we 
recommend that students wash their clothes 
regularly and do not submit more than 3 
kilograms of clothes at a time. The service 
provider reserves the right to take only 3 Kg of 
load at any given point of time to ensure 
delivery of the service in time. 
27.7.8 Processing Time. On average, the 
laundry processing time ranges from 
2 to 4 days.

Vijaybhoomi runs an A/C shuttle bus 
transportation for students to commute 
between the University and Karjat 
station. This facility is extended on a cost 
basis. The students can find out the timings 
of the trips and the cost from 
the VP -DORF and/or the warden. The 
students are required to book 24 hours in 
advance to avoid any inconvenience. 
Based on availability of the transport the 
students can opt for special trips 
provided they can meet the cost  of use of 
the transport facility.

the student, Vijaybhoomi has created a 
state-of-the-art Student Portal that the 
student can access anytime, and anywhere.

URL: http://erp.vijaybhoomi.edu.in/

Learning ID. All communication to the institute 
should be sent through the Keep Learning email.

to Office 365 products (Word, Excel, 
PowerPoint, Access, OneDrive for Business,

on your Desktop/Laptop/ Tablet/Mobile. The 
applications would help you in completing 
various assignments provided during the 
course.

personal profile data, fee data, exam 
notification, and term/semester scores 
through this portal.

drop in a mail to

27.11 Keep Learning ERP. 
You will receive access to the system 
once you complete your registration. As a 
student you can do the following: 
 
27.11.1 Register for courses (as, and when the 
course registration opens. You need to 
contact the Registrar/Program Office for 
more information) 
27.11.2 Check Schedule – You can check

your term/semester schedule on the 
ERP. The schedule would inform you 
about the class details (like course name, 
course code, classroom, faculty name, 
date, start, and end time). You can sync 
the schedule to your mobile calendar 
using the Keep Learning Mobile App. 
27.11.3 Check Attendance – You can 
keep a tab on your class attendance for 
each course. This is to ensure you 
always maintain the minimum class 
requirement for the program. You can 
also check this from the Keep Learning 
Mobile app. 
27.11.4 Check marks & grades – 
Vijaybhoomi supports rights to privacy. 
Your marks and grades will be available 
to you on the ERP as soon as they are 
uploaded by faculty or Program Office. 
27.11.5 Pay Fees – You can also pay 
your fees (tuition, hostel, or any other 
type of fees) through the ERP. The Axis 
Bank Easy Pay module is integrated 
with Vijaybhoomi’ s ERP. It gives the 
facility to pay through one of the many 
options like cash, cheque, NEFT/RTGS, 
credit/debit cards, and net banking. 
Once the fee is paid successfully you can 
download the fee receipt from the system.

submit course feedback for each course. The 
feedback is collected twice, once mid of the 
semester/term, and another end of semester 
term. The feedback is completely 
anonymous. The system does generate a 
report of participants who didn’t give 
feedback. For those who submitted the 
feedback, there is no way to find out which 
participant gave what feedback. The 
feedback is reviewed seriously by the 
Vijaybhoomi management, and it acts as an 
input to academic process improvement. 
27.11.7 Once you complete all registration 
formalities you will get access to the Keep 
Learning ERP. You can log-in using the access 
credentials using your desktop or mobile app.

the right to request for submission on paper and 
the instructions of the faculty are supreme. 
27.12.3 All courses may or may not use the LMS 
as this is completely dependent on the faculty. 
27.12.4 Vijaybhoomi has installed lecture 
capture system in most classrooms and the 
recording of the lectures are available on the 
LMS under the registered courses. 
27.12.5 Students are encouraged to use the 
discussion boards of the LMS to discuss 
coursework and work collaboratively with 
other students. Students are required to use 
appropriate language whilst using such 
discussion boards. Use of foul language is a 
punishable offence. Creation of threads that 
are anti-University, anti- national or 
objectionable are a strict no and the 
University has the rights to delete such 
threads as and when detected.

27.13.1 Being online ensures you stay 
connected to all the systems at Vijaybhoomi 
University and stay updated. To ensure 
hassle-free connectivity each student at 
Vijaybhoomi University can connect to the 
Wi-Fi network from Vijaybhoomi University 
Campus or Hostel. You can sign in to the 
Vijaybhoomi University Student network 
using the Keep Learning access credentials.

given point of time, you can connect to

through two devices. If you have 
connected through 2 devices the 
connectivity speed would split between 
both the devices. The University 
endeavors to provide each student 
with 150 GB of data per month and 5 
MBPS connectivity. The throughput is 
computed at an average and the speeds 
of access may vary based on the load 
and usage of the bandwidth. On 
exhausting the 150 GB of data in each 
month, students can opt for additional 
data on a payment basis. Students can 
use this URL to check their remaining 
monthly WI-FI data balance and to 
renew their subscription: 
http://wificustomer.ibustech.com/#/logi 
n

refrain from using streaming services for 
entertainment purposed on the 
network. This would hamper the speeds 
of other users and impact work 
adversely. The IT department reserves 
the right to block any content/site that 
is objectionable and leads to disruption 
of the internet access to users are large.

27.14. Device & Usage policy.  
 At Vijaybhoomi University we follow 
BYOD (Bring your own device) policy. You 
can plug in your laptop/tablet/cell phones 
to Vijaybhoomi University’s network. By 
login into Vijaybhoomi University’s 
network, you would be responsible for the 
data exchange that’s happening through 
the network. The 
network is constantly under surveillance. 
Legally, you are personally, and fiscally 
responsible for any information disclosure 
from your computer or mobile devices, 
whether accidental or not. We are in the process of 
implementing Mobile Device 
Management (which means your device would 
have an app installed which will allow you to 
access Vijaybhoomi University’s network). We 
expect you to respect copyrights, and licenses, 
respect the integrity of computer-based 
information resources, and refrain from seeking to 
gain unauthorized access, and respect the rights 
of other 
information resource users. You are also not 
allowed to download or install any non-licensed 
application (including malware) on your laptop or 
mobile devices. In case you need to download an 
application please get written permission of the IT 
department by               s sending email to 
ithelpdesk@vijaybhoomi.edu.in. The  team 
would help in facilitating the same. 
27.15 Content Usage and Access. 
27.15.1 Accessing pornographic or, and site 
of violence is strictly banned on university 
campus. Use of Deep Web, Dark Web, use 
TOR or similar browser, and Onion Websites 
etc are also strictly banned. Using VPN, 
downloading torrents is also banned. Please 
note access to banned sites, software and 
content is a punishable offence. 
27.15.2 You are also advised not to share 
your email/ any other application access 
credentials with peers. This is to ensure data 
integrity in the system is maintained. You 
are also requested not to use an easy 
password for any of your applications. 
 
27.16. University Email ID, and more 
As soon you complete your registration you 
will receive an official email ID. It’s an Office 
365 ID comes with a lot of

lifelong even after you complete

27.17. Use of Laboratory, Studios, Music 
Performance Rooms, Auditorium etc.

27.17.1 All the facilities of the 
University are accessible by eligible 
students at the University. Guests and 
visitors are not allowed to use such 
facilities unless they have been 
authorized by a competent authority. 
Each of these facilities has their own 
rules and guidelines for use. The 
student is requested to meet with the 
official in charge of such facilities to 
understand the rules and guidelines.                                             
27.17.2 Emergency Aid. In the event of 
an emergency, like fire, theft, 
housebreak, electricity/ water failure, 
etc., the resident Warden has all the 
necessary telephone numbers for 
contacting the appropriate agencies/ 
offices. The warden shall also conduct 
periodic fire drills, and the students 
must participate in the same. In case of 
being stung by an insect/reptile, the 
student is required to report the same 
to the CMO or to the Warden at the 
earliest. 
 
27.18 Cashless Campus. 
Vijaybhoomi University runs a cashless 
environment on their campuses. 
Students can use G-pay, Paytm or any form of 
online payment method, this substantially 
reduces the need for students to hold excess 
cash on campus. Students should refrain 
from using cash to avail themselves of 
services from all the official and empaneled 
service providers on campus. In case any of 
the service providers insists on cash payment, 
the student is required to bring this to the 
attention of the warden immediately. 
 
27.19 Payment of Fees 
 
27.19.1 All students will be required to pay 
their    fee as per the stipulated schedule 
mentioned in their admission offer letters or 
as per the latest notifications of the 
University. The fee must be paid   electronically 
only through the payment gateway accessible 
through   the Keep Learning System. The 
University does not accept cash. Payments made 
through any other mode besides the payment 
gateway of Keep Learning System shall attract a 
processing charge of Rs 5,000 (Rupees Five 
Thousand Only) over and above the stipulated fee. 
27.19.2 Please note the University shall charges Rs. 
1000 (Rupees One Thousand Only) for every day of 
delay starting from the due date of receipt till. 7 
days. The University shall charge Rs 5000 (Rupees 
Five Thousand Only) from the 8th day till the 15th 
day. In case the student fee is delayed beyond 15 
days, the student’s access to the Keep Learning 
System shall be withdrawn automatically and the 
students will be barred from attending classes. 
27.19.3. In case the student is delayed beyond 
thirty days, the student will be automatically 
deregistered from all courses in the current term. 
The students will not be permitted to take exams 
or participate in activities during the term. 
27.19.4 Students will be required to clear their 
dues and pay Rs 25,000 (Rupees Twenty-Five 
Thousand Only) for re- registering during the same 
term if they   want to continue their studies in the 
term.
